caveats: The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and the independent native-local build-core run reproduced the squirreljme_libretro.zip package, resolver metadata, both ABI artifacts, and both active-marker build logs byte for byte. Execution was local; both builds cloned the pinned source over the network, so no offline source cache is proven.

The armhf artifact has no libstdc++ dependency, so it clears every captured provider ceiling; ARM64 is bound to ra64-universal-v1 and ARMHF to ra32-a30-v1. Provider inspection and target-runtime capture are absent, so every device view remains provisional and ineligible pending a runtime smoke result.

Content, BIOS/firmware handling, controls, audio/video pacing, saves and state round trips, reset and unload behavior, frontend integration, compatibility, licensing review, and sustained performance remain target-runtime and human gates. Publication remains disabled regardless of local byte reproducibility.

The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and independent native-local build-core run reproduced the package, resolver metadata, the armhf artifact, and the build log byte for byte. Both profiles used the generic direct-cmake proof; there is no per-core log contract.

The pristine source is commit c8de2e47c2994f1c36215dd29d44fecf086f25ca, tree 6ea2d4410275f5c022594050177e2c18e11f0458, from the canonical SquirrelJME/SquirrelJME repository (the legacy rule's XerTheSquirrel URL is a redirect), with no submodules. SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is pinned to the commit's committer epoch 1784151532.

Three reviewed build overlays are applied to armhf: a one-token upstream fix adding the missing OR in system-map.cmake's ARM32 elseif, and host-compiler pins for the configure-time decode and sourceize utilities, which CMake otherwise builds with the forwarded cross compiler and then cannot execute. The overlays affect configure only; the artifact is byte-identical across both build profiles.
The core is shipped and built armhf-only, matching the SpruceOS baseline. It is the nanocoat C virtual machine's libretro frontend; Java ME describes what it runs, not how it builds.

Content loading (JAR/JAD/SQC), input mapping, audio and video pacing, saves, states, frontend integration, compatibility, licensing review (Mozilla Public License 2.0), and sustained performance remain target-runtime and human gates. Publication remains disabled.
